O.content: The chart shows monthly bars, y-axis ticks, and axis titles, but no visible severity legend, critical cutoff, or routing instruction.

O.location: x-axis at far-right bar and plot area
O.content: The bar attached to "May" is visibly the shortest displayed bar.

B.text: If the chart establishes that May is low-pumping but no supplied policy defines a critical threshold, and the workflow defaults unthresholded low-pumping cases to standard follow-up rather than escalation, then May should receive standard follow-up.
B.conditions: Requires a default-to-standard policy assumption; no such policy is visibly stated or supplied.

O.content: The far-right red bar is attached to the label "May".

O.location: plot area, May and other monthly bars
O.content: The top of the May bar is lower on the page than the tops of every other displayed monthly bar.
The May bar top is below the printed "10,000" y-axis tick, while the other bar tops are above it.
The vertical axis is inscribed "Pumping volume (m3)".

B.text: If the vertical axis labeled "Pumping volume (m3)" encodes pumping volume with higher bar tops representing greater volume, and the routing practice treats an isolated month that is visibly far lower than every other displayed month as a critical low-pumping anomaly, then that month should be escalated.
B.conditions: Applies to the displayed monthly bars; critical-routing convention is an assumption because no explicit severity threshold or routing policy is supplied.
